title: The Day the Sun Stood Still

named.name: Gibeon
named.label: above
named.note: A great city "like one of the royal cities" (v. 2), which had just made peace with Israel (Josh 9). The five kings attack it for that alliance.

named.name: Gilgal
named.label: below
named.note: Israel's base camp near the Jordan. From here Joshua marched all night to Gibeon (v. 9).

named.name: Jerusalem
named.label: below
named.note: Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, called the other four kings together (vv. 1–4).

named.name: Jarmuth
named.label: right
named.note: Piram, king of Jarmuth, was one of the five kings (v. 3).

named.name: Beth-horon
named.label: below
named.note: The "ascent of Beth-horon" (v. 10) climbs from the Aijalon Valley past Lower to Upper Beth-horon, the main pass from the coastal plain into the hill country.

named.name: Lower Beth-horon
named.label: above
named.note: From here the road drops into the Valley of Aijalon: the "descent of Beth-horon" where the hailstones fell (v. 11).

named.name: Azekah
named.label: left
named.note: The pursuit reached as far as Azekah and Makkedah (v. 10).

named.name: Hebron
named.label: right
named.note: Hoham, king of Hebron, was one of the five kings (v. 3).

named.name: Lachish
named.label: below
named.note: Japhia, king of Lachish, was one of the five kings (v. 3).

named.name: Eglon
named.label: below
named.note: Debir, king of Eglon, was one of the five kings (v. 3). Tel Hesi is the main alternative site.

moves.text: The five Amorite kings march on Gibeon and camp before it
Gibeon's messengers ask Joshua at Gilgal for help
Joshua marches all night from Gilgal and surprises them
The Amorites flee by the ascent and descent of Beth-horon
Israel pursues and strikes them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah
Joshua returns with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal

symbols.label: Hailstones
symbols.key: Hailstones on the descent of Beth-horon

notes.h: The two halves of the battle
p: The battle runs west, away from Gibeon and down toward the coastal plain. The road climbs from the Valley of Aijalon past Lower Beth-horon to Upper Beth-horon and on to Gibeon; the fleeing Amorites ran it in reverse, "the ascent" and then "the descent" of Beth-horon (vv. 10–11), toward their own cities in the Shephelah. Azekah and Makkedah lie on that line of retreat.

Joshua's words place the sun over Gibeon and the moon over the Valley of Aijalon (v. 12), about 20 km apart, which fits a speaker near Gibeon in the morning looking east to the sun and west to the setting moon. The text quotes the poem from the Book of Jashar (v. 13). Interpreters differ on whether to read it as a prolonged day, a prolonged darkness or cooling, or poetic language; the map only marks the two places named.

Verse 15 returns Israel to Gilgal, yet verse 21 has the army in camp at Makkedah and verse 43 repeats the return to Gilgal. The Greek Septuagint lacks verses 15 and 43, and many read verse 15 as anticipating the end of the campaign. The return is drawn dotted for that reason.
Gibeon, the Beth-horon road, Azekah and the five cities are located from OpenBible.info. The lines between them are reconstructions drawn for teaching. Gilgal's exact site is uncertain.
